title: The Afternoon Brief: Coaching shakeups, transfer fees, and one word: privilege
dek: The Angels gutted their pitching staff and the Eagles' pass rush stays sidelined, while European clubs kept spending and a growing list of stories tests how sports institutions respond under pressure.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Across baseball, football, and soccer, the day's stories share a common thread: institutions under strain are making visible moves, coaching changes, resignations demanded, injuries disclosed, while the outcomes of those moves remain unresolved.
bottom_line: The day's throughline is institutions responding visibly to strain: the Angels gutted their pitching coaching staff at 45-74, the Eagles' $100 million pass-rush addition remains sidelined indefinitely, and a former FIFA Council member broke publicly with African backing for Gianni Infantino over the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal. Transfer activity continued in parallel, with Fulham, Forest, Manchester City, and Inter Milan all completing or pursuing deals, while HISA opened a formal investigation into five races flagged by bookmakers on both sides of the Atlantic. The honest read is that most of these threads are still open: Stiggers's diagnosis, Bardghji's recovery timeline, the Spence transfer's completion, and CAF's response to Johansen are all unresolved as of today's reporting. Checkpoints to watch include Greenard's practice status ahead of Week 1, the September 1 transfer deadline, and any HISA findings or further African football reaction to Johansen's statement.
body: The Los Angeles Angels, sitting at 45-74, the worst record in Major League Baseball, fired pitching coach Mike Maddux and two assistants on Tuesday, a staff shakeup with seven weeks left in a season already headed toward an 11th straight losing year. The move arrives with the pitching staff ranked seventh-worst in ERA at 4.51 and leading the majors in walks at 508. Interim replacements Tim Leveque and Michael Wuertz now inherit a problem the previous staff could not solve.

Injury news dominated the rest of the day. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Jonathan Greenard, acquired for two third-round picks and signed to a four-year, $100 million extension, will miss at least another couple of weeks with a pectoral strain, and expressed doubt about whether Greenard practices before the regular season despite the team's earlier characterization of the injury as not long-term. Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with Tampa Bay and was hospitalized by ambulance; coach Aaron Glenn said he was conscious and able to speak, though his diagnosis has not been disclosed. In soccer, Barcelona's Roony Bardghji, 20, tore the ACL in his right knee in training, the second tear to the same knee in two years, ruling him out of a planned transfer before the September 1 window closes and sidelining him for months. And Jakob Ingebrigtsen won 5,000m gold at the European Athletics Championships in 13:15.29, returning 324 days after Achilles surgery following just six weeks of training.

The transfer market stayed active in England and Italy. Fulham signed midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton for £30 million on a five-year deal, making him the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever. Nottingham Forest signed defender Ousmane Diomande, 22, from Sporting CP for £34 million on a four-year deal with a one-year option. Manchester City brought back goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille on a two-year deal as backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma. Inter Milan remain in advanced talks with Tottenham for full-back Djed Spence in a deal worth roughly £25.6 million, with no agreement finalized.

On the governance and integrity side, former FIFA Council member Isha Johansen publicly called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign over what she called ethical breaches in the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, becoming the first prominent African football figure to break from the continental backing that has shielded him. The Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority opened an investigation into five races Sunday at Saratoga and Monmouth Park after U.S. and U.K. bookmakers flagged unusual betting patterns and form reversals in horses tied to Fair Hill Training Facility in Maryland, the first time overseas bookmakers have alerted HISA to domestic anomalies. Separately, Comcast and Disney ended a three-month blackout that had kept NFL Network and NFL RedZone off Comcast platforms since late April, restoring the channels ahead of the 2026 season, though financial terms were not disclosed. DiJonai Carrington clarified a social media post following her ejection from a Sky-Fever game, stating she never claimed the foul assessment itself reflected white privilege. And former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck underwent brain scans, blood tests, and cognitive assessments at Boston University as part of an NIH-funded, multi-site effort to develop the first living diagnosis for CTE, a disease confirmed in more than 100 deceased NFL players but undetectable in the living.

The reporting does not connect these threads causally; the Angels' coaching change, the Eagles' injury timeline, and the FIFA dissent are separate stories driven by separate pressures. Where a driver is named, it is specific: the Angels cited pitching performance and record; Johansen cited an ethical line she says Infantino crossed; HISA's trigger was bookmaker-flagged betting anomalies. Where it is not, such as Carrington's underlying intent or Stiggers's diagnosis, the stories say so plainly rather than guessing.
No desk boards were available this cycle, so standings, injury statuses, and figures above rest entirely on the day's published reporting.

The coming days carry several concrete checkpoints. Watch whether the Angels' interim staff moves the walk rate before the season's final stretch, whether Greenard practices at all before Week 1, and for updates on Stiggers's hospital evaluation and Bardghji's surgery outcome. In soccer, the September 1 transfer deadline will resolve the Spence-to-Inter talks and test whether Fulham's and Forest's new signings integrate quickly, starting with Fulham's Chelsea opener. In governance, watch whether other African football officials follow Johansen's public break or whether CAP's unified backing for Infantino holds. And HISA's investigation into the five flagged races will turn on forthcoming drug-test results and any official findings.
